newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM SHOOTS FOR IMMORTALITY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM SHOOTS FOR IMMORTALITY.

text.p: Silver Charm can complete a rags-to-riches saga on Saturday with a victory in the Belmont Stakes that would make him only history's 12th Triple Crown winner.

Sweeping the series is a rare enough accomplishment, even among thoroughbred royalty, but would be truly unique coming from a colt with such humble beginnings that he failed to meet pedigree standards for select sales as a yearling.

The horse that showed the heart and determination of a great champion in winning the Kentucky Derby and Preakness Stakes last month was sold for a mere $16,500 at the 1995 Ocala (Florida) August yearling sale.
Silver Charm's bargain basement price was a result of being born to Bonnie's Poker, an obscurely-bred mare who spent her career in claiming races, and the unfashionably-bred Silver Buck.
But Silver Charm showed early signs of talent as a two-year-old in morning workouts and was purchased by trainer Bob Baffert on behalf of owners Bob and Beverly Lewis for $85,000.
He raced three times in California as a two-year old, losing his debut, then breaking his maiden on August 24 and winning the Grade II Del Mar Futurity by a head.

Baffert, who saddled runnerup Cavonnier in the 1996 Kentucky Derby, lost training time with Silver Charm last winter and was not at all sure the gray colt would be ready for the Triple Crown -- the classic series for the finest three-year-old thoroughbreds.
"I got behind on this horse," Baffert admitted. "He got heavy, then he got sick and then he got fat on me."

Silver Charm made his three-year-old debut in the Grade III San Vincente on February 8, beating Free House by 1 3/4 lengths, beginning a rivalry that would come to a head with the Triple Crown on the line.
Free House won the Grade II San Felipe Stakes on March 16 by 3/4 of a length over Silver Charm, then edged him again by a head in the Grade I Santa Anita Derby on April 5.
That was the last time Silver Charm has been beaten.
On May 3, Silver Charm ran down Free House in the stretch of the Kentucky Derby, then determinedly held off a late charge from Captain Bodgit -- one down and two to go.
In the thrilling finale to the Preakness Stakes on May 17, Silver Charm finished a head in front of Free House, with Captain Bodgit another head back in a photo finish.
A leg injury put Captain Bodgit out of the three-way picture for Belmont and out of racing.
But Free House will be on hand to renew the rivalry in the final and most grueling race of the series -- the 1 1/2-mile Belmont Stakes, which jockey Gary Stevens has guaranteed Silver Charm will win.
Stevens, who has ridden Silver Charm in his last three races, was positively oozing confidence that his mount would become the first Triple Crown winner since Affirmed in 1978.
"The way he's cooled out after (the Derby and Preakness), it was like he hadn't even run in a race," Stevens said.
"He recovered very, very quickly as far as his breathing and he cooled out in each race before we went to the winner's enclosure. That tells me that he's possibly saving a little something."
Stevens admitted to being a bit less confident ahead of the middle leg of the Triple Crown.
"Bob was very nervous before the Preakness which made me a bit uneasy," Stevens said.
"I didn't feel that he had trained him quite as hard for the Preakness as he did for the Kentucky Derby, which to me is genius.
"(Baffert) knew that if he went hard after this horse for both of those races, we probably were going to be sitting on empty for the Belmont Stakes," Stevens said.
"He told me he relied on this horse's class to get us through the Preakness. That's why I guaranteed the win in the Belmont Stakes."
Silver Charm has come a long way and Saturday he has a chance to join the immortals, such as Count Fleet, Citation and the legendary Secretariat.
